ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity white dominates approximately 75% of the visible ventral surface, with high-contrast low-intensity black pigmentation occupying the remaining 25% primarily along the peripheral boundaries and trailing edges.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central regions of both lobes consist of contiguous high-intensity white blobs. Low-intensity black pigmentation forms a continuous border along the leading edge and tips, with segmented, vertical finger-like projections (rake marks) extending into the white field from the trailing edge.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with an estimated internal angle of 55 degrees; notch depth is approximately 15% of the total fluke vertical height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration pattern across the entire trailing edge. Amplitudes of individual peaks vary significantly, with deeper scallops present on the inner half of both lobes near the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave curvature along the trailing edge leading to acute, upwardly-tapered distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive series of parallel, vertical dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) crossing the white ventral fields of both the left and right lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent dark parallel rake marks (orca tooth scarring) covering roughly 40% of the visible white surface area on both lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: Visible yellowish-brown pixel clusters near the fluke notch, indicating potential biological film or localized pigmentation staining.
